content:
Laredo voters overwhelmingly approved Proposition 1 in the 2026 General Election, backing expanded pediatric hospital services in Laredo and Webb County, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The nonbinding advisory measure asked whether the city should support expanding pediatric hospital services and encourage the county to evaluate governmental options under Texas law. Unofficial results showed 48,269 votes in favor — 91.12 percent — and 4,702 against, the Times reported.

The measure does not authorize construction or funding, create a hospital district, or require the county to act, according to the Times. It is a first step: Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño plans to ask Webb County Judge Tano Tijerina to place Proposition 1 on an upcoming Commissioners Court agenda and designate county representatives to work with the city, bringing together local hospitals, pediatric specialists, EMS and families to examine why children are transferred out of town for care. Judge-elect Jerry Garza was also welcomed to take part.

The city has discussed pediatric care for years, the Times reported. In 2024, it explored incentives such as tax abatements, land donations and a tax increment reinvestment zone to attract pediatric investment, including a possible pediatric intensive care unit, and Driscoll Health System expressed interest. Treviño, a physician who worked nearly 40 years at the Health Department, said families now travel hours for specialized care, with costs hitting lower-income families hardest. The next phase is partnerships and funding options aimed at sustaining pediatric inpatient and critical care locally, according to the Times.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Laredo voters approved Proposition 1 with 91.12% of the vote, backing expanded pediatric hospital services — a nonbinding first step toward keeping children's critical care in Webb County.
title: Laredo Voters Back Expanded Pediatric Care in Landslide Proposition 1 Vote
